thesis: Hold. Pre-open pack for this tick is dominated by routine 8-K administrative filings (officer departures, Reg FD disclosures, financing arrangements) with no decision-relevant single-name or broad-market catalyst that fits a conservative core-ETF mandate. The only market-wide item, Morgan Stanley's Mike Wilson saying an S&P 500 correction 'may be exactly what the market needs' while favoring large-cap quality, is a soft, non-directive opinion piece -- not an actionable signal, and acting on a strategist's correction musing would be chasing a headline rather than responding to a dated fact. Context signals (VIX 15.97, calm; 10Y yield 5.268%, elevated; oil/USO down ~2%) support a cautious, wait-and-see regime read but do not by themselves justify a new position under this tier's capital-preservation priority. Book state: sizing equity ~$999.69, cash ~$750.02 (75%), well above the 25% floor, with a single VTI position (~$249.67, ~25.0% of equity) already at this tier's max single-name cap, so any VTI add would breach the 25% limit and any new satellite name would need a real catalyst I don't have today. Consistent with prior lessons showing thin-pack days are best met with holds or sparse action, I propose no orders this tick and will reassess as fresh, dated news arrives.
